title: Reviewing spec changes
summary: In a pull request, spec files are reviewed by what they change in the spec.
description:
A change to the spec is a change to what the product promises. Reading it as a JSON diff hides that: a reworded requirement, a lowered level and a moved file all look like lines.

In a pull request's Files tab, each spec item's file is shown as what changed in that item. Everything else about reviewing a file still applies to it.

stories.as: a reviewer of a pull request
stories.want: to read what changes in the spec as stories and requirements, not as lines of JSON
stories.soThat: I can judge the change without decoding it

requirements.text: Each changed item file is a card showing its changed fields, requirements, figures and lists, in place of its JSON diff. The file's menu switches to the JSON diff and back.
The changes are measured against the commit the pull request's branch started from, not the base branch as it is now. If that commit can't be found, the base branch is used.
Above the files, a summary counts the changed items and requirements and lists what takes something away from the spec. Each entry leads to its item.
A card has the file's viewed state, review verdict and checks, and folds away when viewed.
A changed requirement, field or list takes a comment. The comment goes on a line of the file within that part: one the pull request changed if there is one, on the old side for what was removed.
Review threads and pending comments on the file show at the requirement or field their line belongs to. Those on other lines, and outdated ones, follow the changes.
Comments made on a card and on the JSON diff are the same comments: switching views loses none.
Assets, such as pictures, stay ordinary files.
A pull request that changes the spec has a Spec tab showing only its spec changes: no code files and no JSON diffs. The tab's count is the number of changed parts.
The Spec tab lists the changed parts in the outline's order, each with whether it is viewed, how many comments it has and whether it takes something away, and each leading to its part.

Reworded text shows which words changed. From `layout.spec-split-from` wide the old is beside the new, each with its own words marked; otherwise it is one text with what went out struck through and what came in marked. A setting and a button choose one column in a wide window too.

history.text: In the Spec tab, reworded text reads as one text with what went out struck through and what came in marked, unless the two versions have little in common.
history.reason: One text was hard to compare on a large screen, and applied to the Spec tab only. Old beside new is how a wide window is used everywhere else in the app.

requirements.text: Comments and viewed marks made in the Spec tab and in the Files tab are the same. The Spec tab can be narrowed to the parts not viewed yet, and to those that take something away.

A changed part shows its user stories before its requirements: each added, reworded, deprecated with its reason, or deleted. A deleted story counts as taking something away. Stories take comments like requirements.
Long text is compared paragraph by paragraph and list item by list item. Unchanged paragraphs away from a change are folded into one line that opens them.
A part that is new or gone as a whole reads as plain text, not as added or removed lines. Its long text and all but its first `spec-review.whole-shown` requirements start folded and open on demand.
A requirement the pull request left unchanged takes comments where the pull request's diff reaches its lines. Every comment button says which line of which file the comment lands on.

A changed named value shows what it was and what it is, as each looks, with the reason when one was recorded. A value whose meaning changed without a recorded reason says so, and a deleted value counts as taking something away.

A comparison of two specs lists what is related to something that changed and wasn't changed itself, with what it says now and what it is related to, so that it can be checked. What was dropped isn't listed. A changed `related` list shows what it pointed at before and after.

values.description: How many requirements of a new or removed part show before asking.
